title: Separating app and index
idea: `app.js` builds and exports the Express app; `index.js` imports it and calls `listen`. Importing the app never opens a port.
points: `app.js` creates the app, adds middleware and routers, and exports it.
`index.js` loads the environment, imports the app and calls `listen`.
Imports run first, so import `dotenv/config` before any file that reads `process.env`.
Start the project with `node src/index.js`; running `app.js` alone shows nothing.

steps.caption: `index.js` imports the app. Importing builds it, but opens no port.
Only `index.js` calls `listen`, so only running it opens the real port.
A test imports the same app and starts it on a free port of its own.

pitfalls: Do not call `listen` in `app.js`: every import would try to open a port.
`dotenv.config()` below the imports runs too late for env values `app.js` reads when imported.

quiz.why: Imports run before the importing file's own code, so `app.js` finishes first.

takeaway: `app.js` builds, `index.js` starts: importing the app never listens.
